# Core practices (generated, do not edit)

Generated by `hermes/build_skills.py` from `standards/rules.json`. Change the docs or the registry in
the core repo, never this file. The full docs sit next to this skill in `references/` after a sync.

How to use it:

1. Before a build, fix or review, read the rules for the stacks you touch (the `applies_to` column)
   plus every `all` rule. A `must` rule is mandatory. A `should` rule is the default; deviate only
   with a stated reason.
2. Where the work breaks a rule, fix the work. Where the rule cannot hold for a good reason, record an
   explicit exception in the consumer overlay, never a silent deviation.
3. When the work finds a pattern another consumer's agent would want, knowing nothing about this
   machine, and it carries no name, path or value of this estate, open a plain, sanitised issue for
   it on the core (the `core-improvement-issue` skill; CONTRIBUTING.md "Does it belong in the
   core?"). Anything that fails that test stays local.

## automation-safety.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `automation-safety.1.1` Automation acts only on its owner's own work | must | all | test | A lane, job or session changes only items owned by the account it acts for. Work owned by other people is surfaced to the owner for direction and never fixed, merged, closed, approved or commented on by automation. |
| `automation-safety.1.2` Every write path has a dry run | must | all | test | Each command that writes supports a dry-run or what-if mode that prints the exact actions it would take and makes no write. New jobs ship in dry run first. |
| `automation-safety.1.3` Never smoke-test on real items | must | all | review | Prove a write path with synthetic records, a scratch state directory, a scratch server port and fake binaries. Test refusal guards with an impossible value (an all-zero commit sha). Restore anything touched and label synthetic data as synthetic. |
| `automation-safety.1.4` Re-verify live state immediately before acting | must | all | test | A queued item, UI row or brief is a snapshot. Re-read the object right before the write, pin the version that was reviewed (head sha, run attempt, updated time), and refuse when it moved. Destructive and privileged acts also require a typed confirmation of the object's name. |
| `automation-safety.1.5` Fail closed on read errors | must | all | test | An error, a timeout or a short read is never "nothing there". Nothing is approved, closed or deleted on a failed read, and destructive runs carry a change cap. |
| `automation-safety.1.6` One stable work item per problem set | must | all | test | Raise one item per distinct problem set, with an id from the sorted problem keys, never volatile text. The same set updates in place, a dismissed item stays dismissed until the set changes, and a clean run closes it. A handled decision holds against new keys unless there is new source evidence dated after it; model prose is never evidence. |
| `automation-safety.1.7` Retries are idempotent and bounded | must | all | test | Every action is safe to repeat and treats "already done" as success. One session runs per (object, version, problem), with a daily cap per object and a run budget per session. |
| `automation-safety.1.8` No grace periods that hide failures | must | all | review | Act on or surface a problem the first time it is seen. Debounce only transient infrastructure errors, by counting consecutive failures, never by delaying the first report of a real problem or by timers that hide an item. |
| `automation-safety.1.9` Kill only your own processes | must | all | repo-check | Track the process ids a job starts and stop them by id or process group after checking the command line still matches. Never kill by a name pattern. |
| `automation-safety.1.10` Human gates stay human | must | all | review | Automation never approves its own work, bypasses a red required check, applies a delete or grants access on the owner's behalf. It prepares the evidence and a button, and the owner's click is the sign-off. The one standing exception is the bounded own-PR merge lane (section 8), which may bypass only the approval count. |
| `automation-safety.7` Count floors and an all-or-nothing change cap | should | all | test | A bulk cleanup reads the whole set first and refuses to continue when any paged read is under its floor (1,000 by default), builds the full candidate list before changing anything, and changes nothing when the list is over the cap (25 by default), printing the would-change list instead. |
| `automation-safety.8` The own-PR merge lane bypasses the approval count only | must | all | test | A standing lane that merges the owner's own pull requests may bypass the required approval count and nothing else: never a red, missing or pending check, a freeze, a hold label or a firing escalation. It runs only while its switch is on and logs every bypass. |
| `automation-safety.1.11` An installer replaces a script by renaming a new file into place | must | local-ops | repo-check | An installer or updater replaces a script by writing a new file beside it and renaming it over the old one, and never overwrites a script that may be running. A shell reads a script incrementally from its open file, so rewriting it in place changes the running copy halfway through. |
| `automation-safety.1.12` An automatic lint fix comes from an AST codemod or a vetted rule list | must | local-ops | repo-check | An unattended lint fix is limited to a short list of rules that cannot change behaviour, comes from a codemod that reads the syntax tree and never a regular expression, and a finding it refuses still reaches the pull request. A tool with no autofix is listed in the fix table, not skipped. |
| `automation-safety.1.13` A change freeze holds what can deploy | must | local-ops | test | A change freeze holds the pull requests whose merge can deploy. A pull request that only changes how CI checks pull requests deploys nothing and is not held, judged on both sides of each changed workflow and on every workflow that names a changed script. Anything unreadable, a path outside the CI paths or a workflow that can run on main holds it. |
| `automation-safety.1.14` Who applied a label is read from the newest timeline events | must | local-ops | test | A lane that trusts who applied a label reads the newest labeled events from the timeline, never a list that truncates. A read error means the label is not trusted. |
| `automation-safety.1.15` A green PR the lane never merged is re-run once, then reported once | must | local-ops | test | A pull request that stays green for the stale-ready window and that the lane never merged has its latest CI run re-run once per head, then one alert line. A pull request waiting that long on a review result gets the alert only. |
| `automation-safety.1.16` A sign-off covers every rule hit, is bound to the head, and never covers a destroy or a replace | must | local-ops | test | A held pull request merges only when a recorded sign-off bound to the current head covers every rule hit by its content fingerprint. A plan that destroys or replaces is never covered by a sign-off and always needs a fresh click. |
| `automation-safety.1.17` A reply or resolve from a card fails closed and never tags an automated reviewer | must | local-ops | test | A reply or resolve from a card fails closed on a failed read: nothing is posted and the click returns the error. Automated reviewers are listed on the card and never tagged. A resolve acts as the approver and only on a thread that is open on that pull request. |
| `automation-safety.1.18` Evidence on an approval card is built from system data, never from a model | must | local-ops | test | Evidence on an approval card (the title source, the plan resources, identities, host tables) is built from the run, its plan and the directory, never generated by a model. A failed evidence read never shows as a pass, a page read only peeks at the cache so it never hangs, and the evidence never replaces the approver's click. |
| `automation-safety.1.19` An automatic ticket comment runs only when its inputs changed | must | local-ops | test | An automatic comment on a ticket runs only when its inputs changed, at most a few times a day per ticket, through the owner connection and never a service account token, and it treats the ticket's text as untrusted data fenced from the instructions. |

## ci-cd-release.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ci-cd-release.1` Workflows are pinned and least-privilege | must | all | overlay-ci | Every action is pinned by full commit sha with the version in a comment, images by digest, workflows declare least-privilege permissions, installs use the frozen lockfile, and CI never rewrites it. |
| `ci-cd-release.2` Required checks are required | must | all | review | Each required check name is listed in the merge gate, and a missing check counts as not passed. The required set follows the repo shape (single hub app, monorepo with IaC, docs-only, local ops center) and always includes the core-ci.yml jobs that apply to it. A private term guard in the attribution job builds its terms from fragments (or hashes) and reports kind and place, never the term. |
| `ci-cd-release.2.1` A weekly full-tree lint sweep keeps one issue | should | all | overlay-ci | A repo with a lint step runs a weekly lint of the whole tree (template lint-sweep.yml) that opens one issue labelled source:lint-sweep on the first failure, updates that same issue on later failures, never opens a second, and closes it on the first green sweep. |
| `ci-cd-release.3` Conventional commits drive the version | must | all | overlay-ci | PR titles follow Conventional Commits, squash merges use the PR title, and the version is computed from commit subjects since the last tag. Nobody bumps versions by hand. |
| `ci-cd-release.4` Major dependency updates never auto-merge | must | all | repo-check | Minor and patch updates are grouped and auto-merge once green. Major updates, and 0.x minor updates, wait for a human review. |
| `ci-cd-release.5` The merge gate never runs PR code | must | all | repo-check | Auto-merge reads only PR metadata and check results, merges only when every check on the head sha passed, and pins the merge to that sha. It merges by the repo's declared method, and a scheduled lane merges only a head unchanged since its last pass, one PR per pass. |
| `ci-cd-release.6` Deploys re-run CI and are health-gated | must | all | repo-check | A deploy runs serialized, re-runs CI on the exact commit, takes a pre-deploy backup where there is data, and gates on health reporting the new version and sha before tagging a release. Branch code builds with no environment or secrets and deploys only through a workflow_run stage running main's copy; software shipped to devices releases from main through signed rings with anti-rollback. |
| `ci-cd-release.6.1` The post-deploy smoke retries for a bounded window, then fails | must | all | test | The post-deploy smoke retries for a bounded window (default 5 minutes), passes on the first good answer and fails when the window ends, naming each attempt. A deploy that stays red raises one alert through the notification path. |
| `ci-cd-release.6.2` A deploy goes through a standby slot and swaps | must | web | review | The build is deployed to a standby slot, started and health-gated there on the new version and commit SHA, then swapped into production; the previous release stays in the standby slot and the slot never opens the database before the swap. |
| `ci-cd-release.6.3` The post-swap smoke polls and retries a 500 without a check list | must | all | test | After the swap the smoke polls production for a bounded window and keeps no list of statuses it retries: a 500, 502, 503, timeout or reset is just not yet, and only the end of the window fails the run; a pass needs the expected version and commit SHA. |
| `ci-cd-release.6.4` A scheduled reaper reclaims old slots without trusting the deploy workflow | must | web | test | A scheduled job outside the deploy workflow lists slots from the platform, keeps production and the one previous-release standby, and stops and deletes any other slot older than a stated age, deciding from the platform's list and timestamps, never a record the deploy wrote. |
| `ci-cd-release.7` Rollback rebuilds a tag through the same gate | must | all | review | Rollback rebuilds an existing tag with its own packaging, shares the deploy concurrency group, and health-gates on that tag. |
| `ci-cd-release.8` Off-site backups are encrypted and verified | must | all | review | An off-site backup is verified, encrypted before it leaves, round-trip checked, and never stored or attached in plaintext. |
| `ci-cd-release.9` Every secret is documented | must | all | repo-check | Every secret a workflow reads is listed with where it lives and what uses it, and a workload identity replaces a stored secret wherever the platform offers one. |
| `ci-cd-release.11` Core consumption classes | must | all | review | An ops center takes every core release at once behind its own gate (when its source is a repo with its own CI gate, as a pull request that merges as soon as that CI passes, never waiting for the owner); every other app (product repos, hubs, multi-module shells, vendored copies) changes only through pull requests the owner approves, and nothing is applied to it directly. |

## cmtrace-logging.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cmtrace-logging.13.1` One CMTrace line per event | must | powershell | test | Every log entry is one line in the section 1 shape, with a plain ASCII message that never contains the sequence ]LOG]!>, type 1, 2 or 3 only, and an empty file attribute. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.2` The logger is Write-CMTraceLog with fixed parameters | must | powershell | test | A script defines `function Write-CMTraceLog` copied from section 2, with the parameters Message, Severity (Information, Warning or Error), Component and LogFile, and no renamed or alternative severity names. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.3` The logger writes through .NET and emits nothing to the pipeline | must | powershell | test | The logger appends with FileShare.ReadWrite through .NET calls, never Add-Content, and emits no object to the success pipeline. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.4` A failed log write never stops the script | must | powershell | test | The logger retries a failed write 3 times, then warns once unless $script:LogQuiet is true, and never throws. A null LogFile means logging is off and returns quietly. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.5` Messages are ASCII | must | powershell | test | The logger replaces any non-ASCII character in a message with ?, and scripts put no emoji or box characters in messages. A row of = marks the header and footer. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.6` The log path matches the execution context | must | powershell | review | The log path follows the section 3 table for the account the script runs as: LOCALAPPDATA for a user, ProgramData for an unattended server task, C:\Windows\Logs\Software for SYSTEM. A script launched from a share logs to the per-user local path, never to the share or next to the script. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.7` The log path is declared once and its folder created with .NET | must | powershell | review | LogFile, LogComponent and MaxLogSizeBytes are set once at the top with a timestamped name, and the folder is created with a .NET call so -WhatIf cannot skip it. A creation failure warns and sets LogFile to null. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.8` Unattended scripts take an optional -LogFile | should | powershell | test | A script that runs unattended exposes an optional -LogFile parameter so a test can point at a scratch path. An empty value turns logging off and is never an error. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.9` The log starts with a header and is written continuously | should | powershell | review | The script writes the section 3 header block right after the folder is created (script, version, machine, log path, and the mode when it has one), then logs as it goes. Lines are never buffered and flushed at the end. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.10` Per-run logs are pruned at start-up | should | powershell | review | Timestamped per-run logs are pruned at start-up, and a pruning failure is a warning that never fails the script. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.11` Fixed-name logs roll to .lo_ at a size limit | must | powershell | test | A fixed-name log from an unattended task sets $script:MaxLogSizeBytes, and the logger moves the full file to <name>.lo_ (one generation) and starts a new one. A script that sets no limit never rotates. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.12` Severity is used as defined | must | powershell | review | Information is for steps, counts and decisions, Warning for something unexpected the script survived, Error for an operation that failed or an exit about to be non-zero. A failure the script handled and recovered from is a Warning, never an Error. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.13` Log the exception message and the identifier | should | powershell | review | A failure line carries the identifier of the thing that failed and $_.Exception.Message, not the whole error record or a stack dump. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.14` Every swallowed external-call catch is logged | must | powershell | review | Every swallowed catch around an AD, Graph, device-management, WMI, CIM, MDM, SSO, file-share or registry call logs a Warning or Error. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.15` Component is a short stable noun | should | powershell | review | The default component is set once with $script:LogComponent from a small stable set of short nouns, passed with -Component only where a section differs. It is never left to $MyInvocation.ScriptName. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.16` Runspaces register the logger from its ScriptBlock | must | powershell | review | A background runspace registers Write-CMTraceLog from its ScriptBlock with New-Item Function:\, never Invoke-Expression on .Definition, and writes to the file directly. Only the display line goes through the dispatcher. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.17` Logging is not gated by -WhatIf | must | powershell | test | Write-CMTraceLog is never wrapped in ShouldProcess and the logger and the log folder use .NET calls, so a -WhatIf run writes the log in full. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.18` A trial run logs the preview and its mode | must | powershell | test | In -WhatIf or trial mode each skipped change is logged as Information with a fixed prefix such as WhatIf: would remove ..., and the header records the mode. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.19` Automation scripts support trial mode and set exit codes | must | powershell | test | An automation script supports -WhatIf (SupportsShouldProcess) or a TrialRun switch and sets explicit exit codes: 0 success, 1 unhandled failure, 3010 for reboot required, any other non-zero value documented. A partial result exits non-zero with one Error line per failed item. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.20` The outcome is logged before exit | must | powershell | test | The last line of every run is the END line with the exit code, written before exit. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.21` A discovery script's stdout is exactly one boolean | must | powershell | test | A script whose stdout a machine reads (a device-management CI discovery) returns only $true or $false, sets $script:LogQuiet = $true, and never calls Write-Warning, Write-Host, Write-Verbose, Write-Information or echo on that path. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.22` A discovery script silences every value-returning call | must | powershell | review | Every call that can return a value in a discovery script is silenced with $null =, [void] or Out-Null, and the decision is logged before the boolean is returned. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.23` No secrets in a log message | must | powershell | review | A log message never holds a password, client secret, token, bearer or Authorization header, private key material, a connection string with credentials, SecureString contents or an API key. It records that authentication succeeded and the identity or thumbprint used. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.24` No PHI in a log message | must | powershell | review | A log message never holds PHI or anything that identifies a patient: names, MRNs, encounter or account numbers or dates of birth. Device names, group names, UPNs and counts are allowed. |
| `cmtrace-logging.13.25` Log status and counts, not bodies or listings | must | powershell | review | A script logs the status, the identifier and the exception message of a Graph, REST or SSO call, never a whole request or response body or a URL carrying a token. It logs counts and paths, not full file contents or directory listings, and a bounded excerpt where user text may appear. |

## data-safety-sqlite.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.1` One writer, enforced by a lock file | must | web | test | Before opening the database the server creates a lock file with an exclusive create and heartbeats it. No second process opens the database while the lock is fresh. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.2` Stale takeover only | must | web | test | A waiting process takes over only when the heartbeat is older than the stale limit or the holder is dead on the same host, renames the stale lock aside atomically, and a holder that finds its token replaced stops. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.3` Listen before you lock | must | web | test | The HTTP server listens first and answers 503 starting until the database is open, so platform warm-up succeeds while the old instance still holds the lock. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.4` Journal mode follows where the file lives | must | web | test | On a network file share the database uses journal_mode DELETE with synchronous FULL, and WAL is never allowed there. WAL is allowed on a cloud host only on the host's local disk, with continuous replication and a passing restore test of the replica (section 8). |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.5` Graceful shutdown | must | web | test | On SIGTERM or SIGINT the server stops HTTP and schedulers, checkpoints, closes the database and releases the lock, with a forced exit after a timeout. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.6` Integrity gate on open | must | web | test | The server runs a quick check on open. On failure it copies the files aside, refuses to open the database and stays up returning 503 with restore instructions. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.7` No silent auto-restore | must | web | test | Restoring from a backup happens only when explicitly enabled, because it discards every write since that backup. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.8` Verified app-level backups | must | web | test | Backups use the online backup API, each copy is verified with a quick check, and they run on startup, nightly, on demand and before every deploy. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.9` Only the app opens the live database | must | web | review | No script, tool, route or console session opens the live database file. Ad hoc inspection uses a backup copy. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.10` Deploys are serialized and health-gated | must | web | repo-check | Deploy and rollback share one concurrency group and gate on the health route reporting the new commit sha. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.11` Stop before deploying over pre-lock code | must | web | review | When the running build predates the lock, or its version is unknown, the app is stopped before the deploy and started after it. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.2.12` Migrations are forward-only and additive | must | web | repo-check | Migrations only add tables, columns with defaults and indexes. Older code must keep working against the newer schema. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.7.1` Server databases: managed identity sign-in | must | web | review | People and apps sign in to a server database with directory tokens or a workload identity; a remaining app password login has no superuser, an owner, an expiry and a place in the secret store. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.7.2` Server databases: retention and restore drills | must | web | review | Backups are kept for the owner-set period, geo-redundant where data cannot be rebuilt, and restored into a scratch database on a schedule with the result recorded in a repo runbook. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.7.3` Server databases: a migration screen in CI | must | web | test | CI fails a migration that drops, truncates, deletes, renames or changes a column type unless it is an approved exception with its reason. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.7.4` An audit log is a serialised, keyed chain | must | web | test | Audit entries are appended under one lock, read the tip by sequence, store a keyed hash of the previous hash plus their content, are written by one shared module and checked by a verify walk. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.8.1` Local-disk WAL keeps the DB, wal and shm off any share | must | web | test | An app that runs WAL on a cloud host keeps the DB, its -wal and its -shm on local disk, and startup refuses WAL when the DB directory is a network filesystem. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.8.2` A snapshot chain plus shipped WAL frames replicate to blob storage | must | web | test | The replicator writes a base snapshot through the online backup API, ships WAL frames in order as separate blobs and starts a new snapshot on a schedule; it never copies, opens or locks the live file. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.8.3` Sealed blobs fence out an old writer | must | web | test | Each blob is created once and never overwritten, and a new lock holder seals its predecessor's chain generation before shipping, so a process that lost the lock cannot extend the chain. |
| `data-safety-sqlite.8.4` A passing restore test of the replica comes before local WAL | must | web | review | A restore of the newest snapshot and following frames into a scratch file passes quick_check and matches row counts and a content hash before the DB moves to local WAL, and reruns on a schedule; a failing or missing result puts the app back on DELETE mode. |

## docs-and-changelog.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `docs-and-changelog.1.1` Done means documented | must | all | review | A change is done when its docs in the docs home match the shipped behaviour, in the same PR when the docs home is the repo, otherwise the day it ships. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.2` One docs home per thing, and one page set per home | must | all | review | Every distinct thing a team runs has exactly one home in the docs home, with an overview, a runbook and a changelog. A repo whose docs home is elsewhere points to it from its README. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.3` One changelog per app, versioned and dated | must | all | overlay-ci | Each app keeps one changelog in its docs home. Every shipped change adds an entry headed with the date and version (## YYYY-MM-DD (vX.Y.Z)), unreleased work sits under "Pending release", and the release record is the version tag plus the entry. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.4` Claims are verified against code and live state | must | all | review | Every behaviour, setting and UI label a doc states is checked in the code and the running system before it is written. A doc that claims a stronger guarantee than the code gives is a defect. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.5` Coverage is audited against a registry | must | all | review | A registry lists everything the team runs with its tier, docs home, changelog and release source. A deterministic audit compares it with the docs home and raises gaps on the owner's documentation view, not on the operational action queue. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.6` Security gaps go to the risk register, not to published pages | must | all | review | A weakness found while documenting is logged as risk and raised to its owner. Once the owner accepts a design, the page states the real trust model plainly. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.7` Retired things keep their history | must | all | review | Retiring a thing marks it retired in the registry, adds a note at the top of each page (date, replacement, where any data export lives) and a final changelog entry, and keeps the pages. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.8` Publishing is idempotent and single-flight | must | all | test | Whatever writes approved pages to the docs home runs one instance at a time under an exclusive lock, records each page the moment it publishes, looks the title up before every create and never creates a page that already exists, and checks that the created title came back unchanged. The coverage audit raises a gap for any title that appears twice in the docs home. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.9` One changelog entry per pull request, append-only | should | all | overlay-ci | A repo whose docs home is the repo adds exactly one changelog entry per pull request, newest first, with the fixed heading ## YYYY-MM-DD (vX.Y.Z[, theme]) or ## YYYY-MM-DD (no version change[, theme]) and at least one bullet, and never edits an older entry. A pull request that only refreshes the core sync paths in the overlay needs no entry. |
| `docs-and-changelog.1.10` Release notes come from the pull request body | must | all | test | Only a `Changelog:` line in a pull request body reaches the generated release notes. A commit of type docs, test, ci, chore, style or build is ignored, and a release with no such line carries one generic line. |

## iac-governance.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `iac-governance.1.1` Everything is declared in code | must | iac | review | Every resource and setting in the managed scope is in code. Console and CLI changes are break-glass only and are back-ported within the back-port window (parameter, default one business day). Existing resources are adopted import-first: a pure-import plan, then an empty follow-up plan. |
| `iac-governance.1.2` State lives in a dedicated, locked backend | must | iac | review | State is remote, in a store that holds nothing but state, reachable only by the plan, apply and break-glass identities, with versioning, soft delete and a delete lock. Applies take the state lock. PR plans run read-only without it, and nobody force-unlocks a lock they did not take. |
| `iac-governance.1.3` Every PR plans, and applies use only the reviewed plan | must | iac | review | Each PR runs format, validate, lint and plan for every root it touches and posts the plan. Applies run from main with the saved, reviewed plan behind an environment approval, never -auto-approve on an unreviewed plan. |
| `iac-governance.1.4` Plan runs auto-approve only for low-risk diffs | must | iac | test | A gated plan run is approved automatically only when the diff cannot change what the pipeline executes or reads. Changes to workflows, code owners, backend or CLI config, external data sources, local or remote exec, non-allowlisted providers or module sources, and diffs too large to read wait for the owner. |
| `iac-governance.1.5` Deletes are guarded and released explicitly | must | iac | review | A plan with any delete or replace fails the normal path. Deletes apply only through an explicit release path (a destroy workflow from main in a protected environment with a typed confirmation) whose plan equals exactly the deletes the PR approved. |
| `iac-governance.1.6` Delete-time guards land before the removal | must | iac | review | Provider flags checked at delete time are read from prior state, so a guard is applied in its own PR before the PR that removes the resource. |
| `iac-governance.1.7` Roots that govern the pipeline are owner-applied | must | iac | review | Roots that create pipeline identities, grant roles, set policy or manage the state backend are applied only by an owner identity, never by the pipeline they govern. |
| `iac-governance.1.8` Drift is detected nightly | must | iac | review | A scheduled plan per root with a detailed exit code, plus a coverage sweep that compares live inventory (child objects included) with state, opens one work item per drift set. |
| `iac-governance.1.9` Change freeze windows block applies and deletes | must | iac | review | Applies, destroys and releases check the freeze calendar (parameter) read live on each run, and fail closed when it cannot be read. |
| `iac-governance.1.10` Providers and modules are pinned | must | iac | review | Provider versions are pinned and the lock file is committed. A new provider address or a module from outside local paths and the allowlist is a held change. |
| `iac-governance.1.11` Owner applies never delete open work's objects | must | iac | test | Before applying a saved plan of an owner-applied root, a guard compares every planned delete with the resources that open pull requests declare in that root and refuses on a match unless the owner names that pull request as meant to lose them. Branch-applied changes to an owner root merge before anything else applies that root. |
| `iac-governance.7` Hash-checked plans, split deletes, placeholder vendor secrets | must | iac | test | A saved plan carries its sha256 and one-day retention and the apply refuses a mismatch; the apply workflow fails any delete or replace, which go through a destroy workflow that lifts and recreates only the needed locks; vendor secrets are IaC placeholders with value-set, owner and expiry tags and ignore_changes on the value. |
| `iac-governance.1.12` An owner apply never undoes what an open pull request applied from its branch | must | iac | test | When a pull request applied an owner-applied root from its branch, the main plan that would destroy or replace what it applied is marked ahead of main and refused until main contains the merge commit, marked or not. An unreadable pull request keeps the hold, and one left ahead for more than two days becomes an item. |

## identity-and-people-data.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identity-and-people-data.1.1` The directory is the source of truth for identity | must | web | review | The identity provider directory owns object id, display name, email and job title. The app stores a cached copy, never a competing one. A fallback copy of the last directory pull is allowed when it is read only if the directory pull fails and is marked stale on screen; the directory pull wins whenever it succeeds and no copy is edited by hand. |
| `identity-and-people-data.1.2` One roster | must | web | review | A single team_members table is the only list of people and every feature links to it by member id, any stable key the directory supplies. |
| `identity-and-people-data.1.3` Directory-only adds | must | web | test | New members are added only by picking a user from the directory, and adding is refused when the directory is unavailable. |
| `identity-and-people-data.1.4` Never fabricate people from name-only data | must | web | test | A seed, import or migration with only a name does not create a member. |
| `identity-and-people-data.1.5` Nightly sync with confident matching | must | web | test | A scheduled sync matches by object id, then exact email, then exact display name when safe, and an ambiguous match is marked unmatched and changes nothing. |
| `identity-and-people-data.1.6` Safe propagation | must | web | test | A confident match overwrites team_members without blanking fields, linked snapshots are fill-only, and past schedule rows, swap audit and OOF entries are never rewritten. |
| `identity-and-people-data.1.7` Test data is synthetic | must | web | repo-check | Fixtures and seeds use made-up people on example.test, never real staff. |

## live-actions.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `live-actions.1.1` Success removes the object at once, everywhere | must | all | test | When the action endpoint returns success, the client removes the object from the shared store that every list, tab and badge reads, and shows a success flash. It does not refetch the list to decide what to show. |
| `live-actions.1.2` A server-side tombstone keeps it gone | must | all | test | On success the server records a tombstone keyed by object and version (for example pr:<repo>#<n>@<head sha>) with the action, the expected end state and a TTL. Every list endpoint hides a tombstoned object until a read shows the expected state or the TTL passes. |
| `live-actions.1.3` A tombstone that expires unconfirmed resurfaces the object, flagged | must | all | test | When the TTL passes and the backend still shows the old state, the object returns with a note that the last action did not land, and the event is logged. |
| `live-actions.1.4` Every write invalidates every cache that holds the object | must | all | test | The action handler clears the cached list, count and detail entries that include the object before it responds. |
| `live-actions.1.5` "Already done" is an idempotent success | must | all | test | When the backend answers already merged, already closed, already in that sprint, already in that status or gone after a delete, the server confirms with a direct read and returns success with already: true, records the tombstone and shows no error. |
| `live-actions.1.6` Confirm through the direct read, never the search or list API | must | all | review | Verification after an action reads the object itself (a pull request by number, an issue by key). Search and list endpoints lag direct reads by seconds to minutes and are used only to build lists. |
| `live-actions.1.7` Actions carry the version the operator saw | must | all | test | The request names the object and the version on screen, the server re-reads live state, and a moved version returns 409 "Refresh first" with no write. |
| `live-actions.1.8` In-flight polls never resurrect | must | all | test | A poll response from a request that started before the latest successful write is dropped, or it passes through the same tombstone filter as the server. |
| `live-actions.1.9` Asynchronous acceptance is a pending state, not a removal | must | all | test | When the backend accepts the action for later (a merge queue, auto-merge, a dispatched workflow), the row moves to an in-flight state with a live indicator and no actions, and it disappears when a direct read shows the end state. |
| `live-actions.1.10` Badges and counts read the same filtered source as the page | must | all | test | Every badge counts from the store the page treats as authority, after tombstones and the page's own filters. |
| `live-actions.1.11` Actionable means the action would go through now | must | all | test | The server decides each object's phase from the same live preconditions its action handler checks, and the client renders buttons only for needs_action objects, never from a raw status field. |
| `live-actions.1.12` Upstream drift redoes the work by itself | must | all | test | When an upstream change invalidates a precondition, the server starts the refresh itself, once per new upstream version, and shows the object in flight until it lands. |
| `live-actions.1.13` Every needs-action object carries a way forward | must | all | test | An object counted as needing the operator has at least one action that moves it. Objects nothing can act on are in flight or not shown. |
| `live-actions.1.14` Unknown never hides | must | all | test | A failed live read leaves the object actionable and the handler re-verifies at click time. Live reads are cached briefly and refreshed in the background. |

## local-ops-app.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `local-ops-app.1` Local ops apps read and draft, never act unasked | must | local-ops | review | A local ops app reads other systems and shows or drafts. It never sends or changes anything on the operator's behalf without an explicit action in the UI. |
| `local-ops-app.3` A neutral contract with a conformance check | must | local-ops | review | State files and the HTTP API are specified in a neutral contract with a schema per file or section, each state file has one named writer and is written atomically, and contract changes update schemas, fixtures and tests together. |
| `local-ops-app.4` Model calls only behind a cost gate | must | local-ops | test | Collectors never call a model. The analyzer calls one only through the gate (forced, daily audit, retry after failure, or a changed bundle past the floor), treats input as untrusted data with no tools, and produces drafts only. |
| `local-ops-app.5` Noise is filtered before the spool | should | local-ops | review | Filtering happens in the collector before the spool, rules are data in the local config, and spool and log sizes are bounded. |
| `local-ops-app.6` The server is loopback only | must | local-ops | test | The server binds 127.0.0.1 only, rejects a Host that is not loopback, rejects a write whose Origin is not loopback, serves only its built assets, sends nosniff, and marks people data no-store. |
| `local-ops-app.7` Read-only modules degrade per section | must | local-ops | test | Each section of a read-only status module fails on its own inside a successful envelope, results are cached per key and served stale while one background refresh runs, every external command runs through one helper with a timeout, and other systems are opened read-only. |
| `local-ops-app.8` Runtime and state live outside the checkout | must | local-ops | review | The service runs a copied runtime outside protected folders, and the state directory and local config live outside both the repo and the runtime, so a deploy never touches data. |
| `local-ops-app.9` Interactive sign-in, never device code | must | local-ops | review | Directory API access uses an interactive authorization-code flow with PKCE and the least delegated scope. Device-code flow is not used. Token files are mode 0600 and never committed. The first sign-in runs in a background tab of a dedicated browser profile, never takes focus, and prints only an MFA number match. |
| `local-ops-app.10` The CI minimum runs and gates merges | must | local-ops | review | The repo runs the CI/CD standard minimum: ASCII, workflow lint, secret scanning, the language test jobs and the PR title check, all required by the merge gate. |
| `local-ops-app.11` Parallel changes use worktrees | should | local-ops | review | Each change gets its own worktree and branch off the remote main, and the main checkout stays clean and on main. |
| `local-ops-app.12` Every gate runs before a PR | must | local-ops | review | The unit tests, the conformance check, the ASCII check and the app typecheck, lint, test and build all run locally before a PR, and CI runs the same set. |
| `local-ops-app.14` Local ops apps wear indigo | must | local-ops | review | Local operations apps set data-app-accent="indigo" on the root and withhold violet from data. |
| `local-ops-app.15` No request waits on an external call once warm | must | local-ops | test | List endpoints serve stale-while-revalidate with single-flight refresh, live checks refresh in the background, every poller fits a per-upstream rate budget, one shared poller per dataset with a server-side badges endpoint, pollers pause on hidden tabs, routes load on demand, responses are compressed with ETag revalidation, and connections stay alive. |
| `local-ops-app.16` What reaches the action queue is routing data | must | local-ops | test | Collectors emit one candidate shape and ordered data rules route every candidate and analyzer item. A person who addressed the operator directly is considered when no rule names them, every must-consider candidate ends as an item or a drop reason, and a route-elsewhere click writes the rule. The prompt carries no routing rules. |
| `local-ops-app.17` Heartbeat watch for every host job | should | local-ops | test | A scheduled job on the host that goes silent or fails raises one action item keyed by job, which clears itself when the job recovers. |
| `local-ops-app.18` Runner-lost alert and recent failures | should | local-ops | test | A run queued with no runner past N minutes raises an item, and cancelled and timed-out runs count as failures in a recent-failures view. |
| `local-ops-app.19` Core consumption panel | must | local-ops | test | The ops center renders a Core consumption panel from consumption.json: per consumer the pin, behind count, sync pull request and CI, status counts, UI verdict and adoption suggestions with risk, plus the account's awaiting and approved-unopened items and the peers' shipped suggestions; each approval is one action through the pull request or issue-comment path only. |

## notifications.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `notifications.1` Pure signal, plain language, no sensitive content | must | all | review | Send only failures and things that need action, in plain words, in first person where the message speaks for the owner, with no AI or tool attribution, no PHI, identifiers or credentials, and never a change to what is sent to other people. |
| `notifications.2` HTML parse mode, no banned characters | must | all | review | Messages use HTML parse mode with only <, > and & escaped, and the formatter strips em and en dashes, curly quotes and other banned characters. |
| `notifications.3` Messages follow the standard layout | must | all | review | Every message uses the layout: severity icon and bold headline, time line, plain-language body, next step, collapsed facts and log excerpt, read-only buttons, capped at 4096 characters. |
| `notifications.4` Severity levels have fixed icons and sounds | must | all | review | Critical, failure, warning, recovered and info use the documented icon and sound, and recovered is sent only after an earlier alert for the same key. |
| `notifications.5` Alerts are deduplicated per key and recover | must | all | review | The same severity for the same key is suppressed for 15 minutes (critical), 1 hour (failure) or 6 hours (warning, info), and a recovered message is sent only when an alert was open. |
| `notifications.6` Delivery goes direct to the owner and never raises | must | all | review | Send goes by direct Bot API call to the owner chat only, with the token read at runtime and never printed, falling back from rich with buttons to rich to plain text, and a delivery failure never raises into the calling job. |
| `notifications.7` Scheduled jobs run under the guard | must | all | review | Scheduled jobs run through the guard wrapper, which sends one formatted alert on failure, preserves the exit code and avoids a second plain failure notice. |
| `notifications.9` Email goes through one renderer behind a CI guard | must | all | test | Every email a tool sends goes through one block renderer: a fixed-width card, callouts without edge bars, a subject naming the change and item, lists capped at 12, public-hostname links and [TEST] self-tests to the sender only. A CI guard fails hand-built email HTML and platform-host links. |

## ops-center-layout.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ops-center-layout.1.1` Group by what we run, never by data source | must | local-ops | review | Group by what we run, never by data source. One hub per domain, with a tab per thing operated. Related operational views are not split across pages by where their data comes from (builds on one page, infrastructure on another). |
| `ops-center-layout.1.2` Sections when a hub has more than about five items | must | local-ops | review | Sections when a hub has more than about five items. The top row is Overview plus titled sections; the second row is one tab per item in the open section. The route shape is `/<hub>/<section>/<item>`. The Overview groups its cards under the same section titles in the same order. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.3` The Overview is one card per item | must | local-ops | test | The Overview is one card per item. A card shows a tone pill (healthy, worth a look, needs me), a one-line headline that leads with the item's live facts (versions, runners online, spend against the projection, not a bare "Healthy"), at most four detail lines, and a link to its item. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.4` One source of truth for counts | must | local-ops | repo-check | One source of truth for counts. The rail badge, the section and item tab counts and the Overview all read one server-side problem list, counted one per problem line (two failing jobs and a stale heartbeat read 3). The client applies no thresholds of its own: none on a count, an age or a duration that decides a tone reporting a problem. Work in progress shows as a spinner, never red, on any item. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.5` Current state and history are different things | must | local-ops | test | Current state and history are different things. A pipeline counts as failed only while its newest finished run on the default branch failed. Older runs fold under History, so a fixed failure never reads as current. A running build is never red, and a cancelled or superseded run never counts. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.6` Newest first everywhere | must | local-ops | test | Newest first everywhere. Cards are ordered by latest activity with running items on top, runs by finish time, scheduled jobs by last run. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.7` Every runnable thing has a start button in the UI | must | local-ops | test | Every runnable thing has a start button in the UI. Pipelines (Run workflow), scheduled jobs (Run now) and maintenance tasks (a backup, a restore drill) can be started from the item. The form opens with safe defaults (dry run on), says plainly when a run will publish, and the primary button then reads "Run for real". The contract in section 3 is the server side of the button. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.8` Name hubs for the work, not the vendor or the tool | must | local-ops | review | Name hubs for the work, not the vendor or the tool. "Work tracking" instead of the tracker's name, "Pull requests" instead of "Reviews". The tool name stays in subtitles and links. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.9` Old links never break | must | local-ops | repo-check | Old links never break. Every renamed or moved route redirects to its new home and keeps its tab and query string. The app keeps a lock file listing every route it has ever served. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.10` A gate override is scoped, time-boxed and fails closed | must | local-ops | repo-check | A gate override is scoped, time-boxed and fails closed. The expiry is stored with the entry and compared on every read, and a missing, unreadable, foreign-scope or expired store means no override. It lifts only its own gate, covers only the owner's own work, and has one writer and one log, confirmed first. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.11` A card never shows a stale reason after an action | must | local-ops | test | A card never shows a stale reason after an action. Until the next pass of whatever re-checks it, the card says what happens next (for example "freeze bypassed, the lane re-checks within 3 minutes"), never the reason the action just removed. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.12` Known transient failures heal themselves and never count as failures | must | local-ops | test | Known transient failures heal themselves and never count as failures. Each known transient failure has a defined automatic recovery (a stale saved plan is re-planned at once). Only a failure that was not recovered reaches the owner or a repeat counter; real failures keep the normal path. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.13` A status card shows unknown when its source is missing, stale or unreadable | must | local-ops | test | A card that depends on a collector's status file shows unknown when the file is missing, older than its limit, unreadable or not the expected shape, and never shows in sync. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.14` A lapsed sign-in nobody renewed is never silent | must | local-ops | test | A collector that needs a signed-in tool keeps serving its last reading marked stale when the sign-in lapses and exits non-zero once the lapse has lasted its limit (default 240 minutes), so an alert fires. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.15` A job that stays red is raised on the board | must | local-ops | test | A failed newest run of a watched deploy workflow on main, and a streak of failed scheduled runs of a nightly workflow, each raise one item naming the failed job. A later success closes it. Cancelled, skipped, manual and branch runs never count, and a watch that cannot be read is itself an item. |
| `ops-center-layout.1.16` A change that takes minutes to reach its destination shows its rollout where it is reviewed | must | local-ops | test | A change that applies at once but takes minutes to reach its destination (an edge, a cache, a fleet) shows its in-flight rollout where the pull request or the apply is reviewed: what is still rolling out, how long ago the change applied, and when it is expected to land, so a reader does not test the old behaviour and call the change broken. |

## pr-review-and-merge.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.1` Commit only the files you changed, by name | must | all | review | Stage and commit with explicit paths (git add -- <files>, git commit -- <files>), from a worktree per change. Never git add -A, git add . or git commit -a. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.2` Conventional Commits for every commit and PR title | must | all | overlay-ci | Types and the semver mapping follow CI/CD section 3. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.3` Every change carries its changelog entry | must | all | overlay-ci | The same PR adds a dated, versioned entry in the changelog of the thing it changes, in the docs home (Docs and Changelog). |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.4` No tool attribution, owner identity only | must | all | overlay-ci | Commits, PR text and comments carry no assistant or tool attribution and no generated-by lines, and commits use the owner's approved address. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.5` The main branch is protected | must | all | review | Nobody pushes to main. Changes land by PR after the required checks pass, by squash or rebase, through a ruleset or the auto-merge gate. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.6` Merges are pinned to the reviewed head | must | all | repo-check | Every merge names the head commit that was reviewed (--match-head-commit <sha> or the API sha field, which must be in the merge call statement: the call, its continuation lines and the body built for it), and every push and merge re-reads the PR state immediately before it runs. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.7` Review findings are verified, not obeyed | must | all | review | Check each finding against the code, fix every real one, refute the rest with evidence (path and line, a run log, live state), and post one disposition reply per round. Stop pushing when the only findings left are re-raises already answered. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.8` A triage marker attests to one head | must | all | test | A triage reply ends with a hidden marker naming the head sha and the finding ids it answers (<!-- triage:<sha> H1 H3 -->). The merge lane clears only the ids named, so a reply that answers one finding never clears another, and a marker with no ids clears nothing. Post it only after that head's review is in, and never on a reply that promises a fix. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.9` Policy holds go to the owner, problems go to the fixer | must | all | test | A hold that needs a person's sign-off (a policy rule, a delete, an access grant, a gate that fails only because a change is intended) shows an approve button. A real problem (red check, conflict, untriaged finding) goes to the fixer and never shows a merge button. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.10` Working PRs get no action buttons | must | all | test | While checks run, a review is pending or a fix session is on the PR, the UI shows a working indicator and only a link to the PR. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.11` Delegated work is verified before merge | must | all | review | The reviewer of work from a sub-agent, a bot or another account re-runs the checks locally (including private ones CI cannot run), reads the full diff and lists the PR's commits. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.12` Never weaken a gate to get green | must | all | review | A fix never lowers a threshold, adds a skip marker or ignore glob, or edits a review policy, workflow or ruleset to pass. A check that is red for an unrelated infrastructure reason is rerun (failed jobs only) and stays red until it passes or the owner bypasses it. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.13` Preflight runs every gate before the push | must | all | test | Before a change is pushed or its PR opened, one local command runs the repo's tests, linters and builds, hygiene checks, a base conflict check, the merge lane's policy rules as a dry run (printing the owner sign-offs for the PR description) and an overlap check against other open changes. It fails closed on read errors with its own exit code and writes nothing outside the git directory. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.14` Self-review uses the reviewers' own prompts and is bound to the diff | must | all | test | The author reviews the full diff against the automated reviewers' prompts plus the finding catalog and records each would-be high or blocking item as fixed or pre-triaged with evidence, in a file whose first line names a hash of the current diff. The preflight fails until the hash matches, so a changed diff needs a fresh self-review. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.15` Infrastructure noise is re-run, bounded and named | must | all | test | Refines rule 12. The merge lane re-runs failed jobs only, without a fix, only when every failed job's log tail matches a known infrastructure-noise pattern, at most a fixed number of times per head (parameter, default 2), and logs the matched pattern. Any failure it cannot name goes to the fixer. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.16` Deletes owned by another open change wait on it | must | all | test | When a plan deletes objects this diff does not touch and another open change by the same owner declares them (it applied them from its branch), this change waits on that one and re-arms (rebase) once it merges. It is never offered as a delete sign-off. A read failure or an undeclared delete keeps the normal sign-off hold. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.17` A fixer that needs the owner returns a decision, and real findings feed the catalog | must | all | test | A fixer that stops on an owner-only choice returns a question, two to four options each with an action kind and its exact effect, and a recommendation. The UI shows one button per option pinned to the reviewed head, and the click signs off that head only. Text posted as the owner is validated first. Fixed findings the catalog missed are appended to it, deduplicated. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.18` A merge commit carries only a noreply author email, with no account setting required | must | all | core-ci | Only GitHub noreply author emails land in history, with no account setting required. scripts/merge-pr.py builds the squash commit itself with the signed-in account's noreply author and merges it with --rebase; without rebase merging it squash merges and refuses non-noreply commits. CI fails any non-noreply email. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.19` Every file is plain ASCII | must | all | overlay-ci | No tracked text file holds a byte above 127. Binaries, lockfiles and synced core copies are out of scope; existing non-ASCII files get a time-boxed exception per path, never a narrowed check. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.20` Every PR declares what it does to issues | must | all | overlay-ci | The PR body holds exactly one of: Closes, Fixes or Resolves #N; Refs #N plus a Remaining line; or No issue with a reason. Reverts and dependency bots pass, and the consumer parameters name further exempt authors, app authors and repo prefixes. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.3` The review bot is a required check that fails closed | must | all | test | The review bot reads its config from the base branch, an override covers one commit, and the check fails only on a confirmed block or a missing review for the head. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.4` Trust holds, and a failed lookup holds | must | all | test | A review lane that merges other people's pull requests holds for the owner the first PR of a new app, a PR by an author with fewer than N merged PRs, and a PR touching device-shipped paths, even when every gate passes. When the lookup a trust hold needs fails, the PR is held. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.21` Merge the latest main and run every check script before a push | must | all | test | Before a push, merge the latest default branch into the branch and run every check script that can run locally: commit subjects, attribution and the private term guard, author identity, ASCII, the changelog entry and the repo checks. A check that runs only in CI is found too late. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.22` A cancelled run is neither a pass nor a failure | must | all | test | A merge gate reads the newest run of each check. A run that a later push or a label edit cancelled is not a failure and never blocks a head that has a later green run; a head whose newest run was cancelled is re-run, a bounded number of times, instead of waiting for someone to re-run it by hand. |
| `pr-review-and-merge.1.23` A PR watch has a stop point and a report | must | all | test | Watching a pull request after it opens is a step with a defined stop: merged, checks failed, closed without merging, a merge conflict or a timeout. It prints a line at every change and ends with a report that names which stop it reached and what to do next. |

## rbac.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rbac.1.1` The server is the access boundary | must | web | test | Every route enforces access on the server. Client permission checks only show or hide UI and are never security. |
| `rbac.1.2` Deny by default | must | web | test | Signing in grants nothing. Access comes only from a grant to the user or one of their groups. |
| `rbac.1.3` Every route declares its guard | must | web | review | No route ships without a declared guard (a permission, signed-in only with a reason, or public with a reason). A check walks the mounted route table and fails on any route without one. |
| `rbac.1.4` No escalation | must | web | test | Nobody can grant a role, change a grant, or create or edit a role that involves a permission they do not hold. |
| `rbac.1.5` Least privilege with real granularity | must | web | review | View is separate from write, sensitive reads are separate from ordinary reads, and no route uses a broad admin right when a narrower one fits. |
| `rbac.1.6` Effective access is an additive union | must | web | test | Effective access is the union of every matched grant (direct and through groups). No grant removes access granted by another. |
| `rbac.1.7` Access changes are audited | must | web | test | Every access change is audited with before and after values, and every RBAC denial records the missing permission. |
| `rbac.2` Permissions come from one catalog | must | web | review | Every permission is registered once in a shared catalog with key, label, description and group. A permission not in the catalog cannot be assigned, and a check fails when the catalog and the enforced permissions differ. |
| `rbac.3` Guards come from one module | must | web | repo-check | Routes use the shared guard helpers only, and handlers decide record access with the shared evaluator, never by comparing permission strings by hand. |
| `rbac.4` Scopes are enforced or not grantable | must | web | test | Only scope kinds a route actually checks can be granted, so a scoped grant never silently grants nothing. Ownership is a permission pair (the base action and its .others variant), not a scope. |
| `rbac.5` Grants are data with an expiry | must | web | test | Roles and grants live in the database, grants map a user or group object id to a role, and an expired grant is ignored at resolution. |
| `rbac.6` View-As is read-only and exact | must | web | test | Impersonation runs on the server, is bound to the admin who started it, expires, rejects every write, and skips ownership exceptions so the preview shows exactly what the previewed role sees. A preview never exceeds the viewer's own permissions (403 and an audit row), and stored roles that hold retired permissions are flagged and stripped on save. |
| `rbac.7` The client uses the shared evaluator | must | web | review | The client has one permission source backed by the same evaluator as the server, and never duplicates server access logic. |

## scripting-powershell.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scripting-powershell.1.1` Workload identity, never a stored secret | must | powershell | review | Authenticate as a managed identity where the host has one, otherwise with a certificate held non-exportable in the machine store. Automation never holds a password, client secret, account key or credential prompt. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.2` Every write path has a trial mode that defaults safe | must | powershell | test | Mutating scripts support -WhatIf or a TrialRun switch. Scheduled and runbook entry points default to trial, and the switch gates every write, including state, ingestion and self-relaunch. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.3` Destructive runs cap and fail closed | must | powershell | test | A script that deletes or disables carries a maximum change count and stops when a source read fails, returns nothing or returns far fewer rows than the last run. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.4` Errors are caught specifically and never swallowed | must | powershell | lint | Wrap each external call in try/catch, catch the specific exception types first, and end with a catch that logs and rethrows or sets a failing exit code. No empty catch and no -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue on a call whose result is used. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.5` Exit codes and output carry the result | must | powershell | review | Exit codes follow CMTrace Logging section 8. Runbooks write results with Write-Output as structured lines or objects, never Write-Host, and end with one summary line of counts. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.6` Names and header are standard | must | powershell | lint | Functions use approved Verb-Noun names, parameters are PascalCase, variables are descriptive, no local variable reuses a parameter name, and no helper shadows a built-in. Every script starts with the header block in section 5. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.7` ASCII only, both editions | must | powershell | overlay-ci | Scripts are plain ASCII and run on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 unless the header names one edition. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.8` Idempotent by design | must | powershell | test | Read current state, change only what differs, read back and verify. A second run of a completed run changes nothing, and keys or folders are created only when missing. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.9` Scheduler parameters are parsed defensively | must | powershell | test | Treat switch values from schedulers and webhooks as strings, normalise with a strict match that keeps trial mode on unless the value is an explicit false, accept parameters the platform may pre-parse from JSON, and anchor validation patterns with \z. |
| `scripting-powershell.1.10` Endpoint scripts respect their execution context | must | powershell | review | Detection only reads and reports, and matches exactly what remediation writes. Scripts assume SYSTEM context, a possibly 32-bit host and repeated retries, and record durable outcomes instead of clock-based limits (section 6). |
| `scripting-powershell.1.11` Runtimes are tracked to retirement | must | powershell | review | Every runbook records the runtime it runs on, and a retirement notice is answered from job evidence with one move to the newest supported runtime. |

## scripting-python.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scripting-python.1.1` Code runs on the interpreter floor | must | python | overlay-ci | The floor is the oldest interpreter that runs the code (parameter, default 3.9 where the OS python is the runtime). Every module with annotations starts with from __future__ import annotations, no newer syntax is used, and CI runs on the floor. |
| `scripting-python.1.2` Standard library first | must | python | repo-check | Use a third-party package only when the standard library cannot do the job, pin it with hashes, and never install packages from inside a script at run time. |
| `scripting-python.1.3` No secrets in argv, environment dumps or logs | must | python | repo-check | Pass secrets on stdin, in a mode 0600 file or by reading the secret store in process. Never log a command line, environment or response body that can carry one, and redact secret-shaped values in errors. |
| `scripting-python.1.4` State files are written atomically | must | python | test | Write to a temp file in the same directory, flush and fsync, then os.replace over the target. Sensitive files are created with mode 0600. Each file has exactly one named writer. |
| `scripting-python.1.5` Scheduled runs cannot overlap | must | python | test | A job that a scheduler starts takes a non-blocking exclusive lock on a lock file and exits 0 with one skip line when another run holds it. The lock is released by process exit. |
| `scripting-python.1.6` Every external path is overridable for tests | must | python | test | State directories, binaries (gh, cloud CLIs) and endpoints come from environment overrides with production defaults. Tests set them inline per command, never exported into a shared shell. |
| `scripting-python.1.7` Tests use synthetic data and pin every fixed bug | must | python | test | Tests run against fixtures and synthetic records, never real ones. Each fixed bug adds a regression case that fails on the old code. |
| `scripting-python.1.8` Subprocesses go through one helper | must | python | lint | Call external commands with an argument list (no shell=True), a timeout, and one helper that turns a missing binary, a timeout or a non-zero exit into an error value. Tests patch that helper. |
| `scripting-python.1.9` Reads fail closed and exits are meaningful | must | python | test | A failed or partial read is an error, never "nothing found". Exit 0 on success, 1 on failure, and other codes only when documented (for example 2 for sign-in needed). |
| `scripting-python.1.10` Lint and format with a committed ruff config | must | python | overlay-ci | pyproject.toml holds the ruff config with target-version equal to the floor, and CI runs ruff check and ruff format --check. |

## secrets-and-credentials.md

| Rule | Level | Applies to | Check | Statement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.1` Identity before secret | must | all | review | Use a managed identity, OIDC workload federation or a certificate whenever the caller and target support one. A stored secret is allowed only when the target supports nothing else, and then it has an owner, an expiry and a place in the secret store. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.2` Grants are least privilege and scoped to the resource | must | all | review | Grant the narrowest role at the narrowest scope (a container or a single resource, not a subscription or a tenant). Narrowing creates the narrow grants first, proves them with a real run, and only then removes the broad grant. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.3` Federated credentials bind to protected environments | must | all | review | A CI federation subject names one deployment environment with required reviewers and a main-only branch policy, never a branch pattern or a wildcard. Each tier has its own identity scoped to its own resources. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.4` Cross-repo CI reads use one read-only deploy key per consumer | must | all | repo-check | CI that must read another private repo uses a deploy key without write access, one per consumer repo, never a personal token. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.5` Secret values never pass through a person or a transcript | must | all | review | Read a secret from the store straight into its destination in one step, test it before the write, compare the read-back by hash without printing, and unset it after. When a person must supply a value, use a masked prompt that names the account and the destination, never chat, a terminal echo or a command argument. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.6` Secrets live only in a secret store | must | all | overlay-ci | Workloads read them at run time with their own identity. Never in a repo, a runbook or pipeline variable, a synced folder, a ticket or a CI log. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.7` Rotation revokes the old value and is planned per consumer | must | all | review | Before rotating, list every consumer, plan the swap for the same minute (some issuers revoke the old value at once on reissue), verify each consumer on the new value, then delete the old credential and purge any soft-deleted copy. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.8` Every PR is scanned for secrets with a hardened scanner | must | all | overlay-ci | Scan the commits of every PR and the default branch with a pinned scanner, using the config from the base commit, with ignore files and inline allow comments disabled, and allowlist known false positives only by path or by an id-shaped match. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.9` Broad grants are an owner decision with a recorded risk owner | must | all | review | A tenant-wide application permission (read-write on all objects, directory, role management, mail, full-control sites) is approved by the accountable owner, with the operational run path described and compensating controls recorded. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.1.10` Accepted long-lived tokens are recorded risks | must | all | review | A token that cannot be avoided records its scopes, owner, consumers and a review date, and revoking it is the documented recovery. |
| `secrets-and-credentials.2` Each caller uses its first-choice identity | must | all | review | Each caller type uses the identity in the section 2 table: managed identity, OIDC federation, device identity, deploy keys, and for a local job calling a user-delegated API, PKCE with a loopback redirect and a 0600 token cache. Device code is never used where policy requires MFA. |
